subject: Dealer Displacement Pricing Accelerator — staged offer and escrow ask
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@retailco.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: vendor displacement economics

Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. RetailCo is running an accelerated procurement window and your performance numbers were compelling — specifically the token latency under 100ms on peak loads. Procurement has asked me to get a clear displacement economics proposal from Redwood so we can compare to our incumbent (VendShift). Two immediate asks from the RFP team: 

- Can you commit to price parity with VendShift's effective blended rate across our current mix (chat generation + embeddings) for year 1, or provide a concrete replacement credit schedule that nets parity?
- We need a short-term operational escrow (3 months) guaranteeing latency/SLOs during and after cutover, plus a performance holdback that sits in escrow until the pilot clears.
- Timeline: decisions by 10/22. We need a term sheet and any standard T&Cs tracked back for legal.

Attached: RetailCo_RFP.pdf (procurement Qs + current usage profile). Please include any proposed migration credits, seat/ingress/egress assumptions, and a DocuSign-ready commercial term if possible.

Best,
Helen Park
Director, Strategic Sourcing — RetailCo
helen.park@retailco.com

Subject: Re: RFP: vendor displacement economics

Helen — really appreciate the clarity and the timeline. Short reply with a staged commercial approach we can deliver quickly: 

Summary (high level)
- Year 1 staged offer: commit to a 12-month agreement with a two-phase credit ladder that nets effective parity against VendShift for months 1–6 via migration credits, then transitions to a 12% unit-rate discount for months 7–12.
- Migration bridge: 3 months of operational credits tied to SLOs (latency and error rate) — those credits live in a holdback escrow and are paid out monthly as SLO checks pass.
- Optional commitment bump: if RetailCo signs a 24-month commitment we can increase the unit-rate discount to 18% and provide an onboarding services credit to cover one week of on-site engineering.

I attached an initial line-item workbook (proposed-credit-schedule.xlsx) with worked examples using the usage profile in your RFP. We can produce a DocuSign-ready commercial term sheet once we agree on the holdback mechanics and the exact parity anchor.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Grace and Priyom will map the net TCO and define the escrow mechanics (holdback trigger windows, measurement telemetry).
2) We ship a draft term sheet + DocuSign link by 10/16.
3) If RetailCo wants to accelerate, we can carve a 6-week pilot with reduced commercial exposure.

Happy to sync 30 mins today if that helps — what time works?

—Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: RetailCo concession structure & escrow design (needs numbers)

Grace / Priyom — looping you both in to land the commercial mechanics. Key asks from RetailCo: price parity (year 1) vs VendShift, a 3-month operational escrow tied to pilot performance, and an expedited term sheet by 10/16.

My proposal (we'll iterate):
- Base offer: 12m term, 12% off list unit-rate starting month 7. Months 1–6 covered by migration credits that are designed to make RetailCo "net whole" vs their incumbent billing.
- Migration credits: defined as $/token credits, paid out monthly from an escrow pool if SLOs are met. Escrow pool size = 6% of estimated 6-month spend (can be adjusted).
- Escrow SLOs: p95 latency < 120ms, error rate < 0.5%, KV cache hit > 60% for generation paths. Metrics must be measured with both parties' telemetry agents to avoid disputes.
- Commitment bump option: 24m -> move to 18% off list + $50k onboarding services credit.

What I need from you: 
- Grace: ops estimate for onboarding week and realistic engineering hours (and whether on-site is feasible given current EMEA scheduling). Also confirm whether legal will require anything fundamentally different for a runtime escrow (I expect a short-term addendum).
- Priyom: commercial model — produce the net-present-value math and a few worked scenarios (6m pilot, 12m with credits, 24m bumped option).

I want numbers by EOD 10/15 so I can fold them into the term sheet for Helen.

Thanks — Mark
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: RetailCo concession structure & escrow design (needs numbers)

Mark / Priyom — quick notes (high level) and attached term mechanics doc.

- Onboarding estimate: 80 engineering hours (remote) + optional 40 hours on-site (travel windows in Nov). On-site adds ~$28k travel+time.
- Escrow mechanics: suggest a rolling monthly escrow verification with a 30-day dispute window. If SLOs fail the month, escrow tranche is retained and applied as credit to RetailCo's next invoice. If SLOs pass, tranche is released to Redwood.
- Escrow pool sizing: agree to start at 6% of 6-month spend (as Mark suggested) — that gives a clear payback runway without overpreserving cash.
- Legal: term sheet addendum is straightforward; we need PS and SLO definitions in the annex. Legal can turn within 3 business days once we hand off the SLO language.

Alternative commercial: instead of immediate parity via credits, propose a two-tier commitment: 12m + 6m pilot = 10% off list after pilot; 24m = 18% off list plus onboarding credit. This reduces cash hit up-front.

Attaching: technical-escrow-term-sheet.docx

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success Operations — Redwood Inference

- Final confirmation on the escrow fund size and exact triggers (we prefer monthly measurement + 30-day cure).
